posts.copy:
Would you write off Pop Mart's US business because one month of card-spend data looked ugly?

In the first half of 2025, its US revenue grew 1,142% year on year, to $315 million. The Labubu blind boxes were real demand.

Then in March 2026, US sales fell 45% year on year on card-transaction data. The online spike cooled about as fast as it built.

What Pop Mart did next reads less like a retreat. It kept signing mall leases. A partnership with Simon Property Group is pushing its US and Canada store count past 60, with more than 20 new mall stores announced.

Its own half-year numbers this August back that up: total revenue up 23.8%, with what the company calls "steady expansion of offline channels" even as overseas growth cooled.

The viral spike got Pop Mart noticed. It did not build repeat customers. That takes a place someone can walk into on a Saturday, a retail relationship, not a moment.

Rebuilding a hype cycle into a habit is most of what our GTM advisory work is for.

We have never worked with Pop Mart. This is commentary from the outside.

Comment CHANNEL and we will send you the three questions we use to test whether a channel converts a spike into a habit.

#GTM #APAC #RetailStrategy #Expansion
posts.sourcePublisher: Pop Mart International Group interim results (primary), corroborated by Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance and Inside Retail Asia
posts.disclosure: We have never worked with Pop Mart. This is commentary from the outside.
posts.verificationNotes: 1,142% YoY US revenue growth to $315M in H1 2025, and the Simon Property Group mall partnership/60+ store count, confirmed via Inside Retail Asia (29 Jan 2026). 45% YoY US sales decline in March 2026 confirmed via Bloomberg Second Measure card-spend data, reported by Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance (29 Apr 2026). 23.8% total H1 2026 revenue growth and the 'steady expansion of offline channels' quote confirmed via Pop Mart's own interim results release (20 Aug 2026). Deliberately did not cite the H1 2026 Americas revenue figure (1.89bn yuan) or its reported -16.5% YoY change, since that percentage traces to analyst commentary layered on the release rather than a figure Pop Mart itself states as a YoY change for that single region.

posts.copy:
August in Hong Kong is supposed to be the quiet month, empty calendars, everyone away.

We pulled more than 150 signups anyway.

Last month we ran summer drinks with Carta and Endowus. Gelato, cold beer, a room of founders and investors.

No panels. No pitch decks. No agenda.

That was the design, not a shortcut. A panel gives forty people permission to sit quietly and watch four people talk. Take the panel away and the same forty people have to actually meet each other, which is the only reason any of them showed up.

Startups do not scale on capital alone. They scale on access, to the right operators and the right partners at the right time. Our job is to keep building the rooms where that happens.

Thanks to Carta and Endowus for co-hosting.

The next one runs alongside the China Tech Trek: Hong Kong and Shenzhen, 13 to 17 October 2026, with ContraVC as official partner.

Comment TREK and we will send you the details.
